Each change is divided by a typical move for its horizon. Moves smaller than a quarter of a typical move are treated as noise and ignored; the result is squashed into −1…+1 and weighted.
Source: Treasury bill curve (a proxy for the expected policy rate). The dashed line is the current policy midpoint.
Current policy is what the Fed has already set. Market-implied policy is what markets expect next. Gold reacts mostly to changes in the second.

The real-yield part of any move is already scored by the real-yield indicator. To avoid counting it twice, this indicator only scores inflation expectations and how high the nominal yield is versus its 1-year norm.
The model scores the surprise (actual − expected), not whether a number is \"good\" or \"bad\". Older releases fade with a 14-day half-life.

Rules: the signal at one day\'s close is traded at the next day\'s close. BUY / STRONG BUY = 100% gold, REDUCE / SELL = cash, HOLD keeps the current position. Only data available on each date is used, and the model version is fixed.

Synthetic prices and scores run through the real signal rules, so the layout can be reviewed. The real backtest arrives in Phase 6. This demo always covers %1$s – %2$s; only the capital you enter is applied.
Bundled illustrative data generated by the real scoring engine. No internet needed; not market data.
Official signals after each US trading day (23:30 UTC), plus live prices and a provisional score every 30 minutes. Data is cached for offline use.
Notifications for signal changes, large score moves, regime changes, major US data releases, Fed decisions and extreme market events arrive in Phase 7.

Gold Signal analyses the main macro drivers of gold (real yields, Fed expectations, the dollar, nominal yields, US data surprises, ETF flows and central-bank buying) and combines them into a transparent 0–100 score. The rules are fixed and versioned, so the same inputs always produce the same result.
Confidence measures agreement between indicators, data freshness, signal persistence and the size of the moves. It is not a probability that gold will rise.
The app never places trades. It is a decision-support tool only.
Turkish and Russian translations should be reviewed by a native speaker before public release.

Share of days on which each indicator had usable data. Missing indicators count as neutral, which pulls scores toward 50.

ETF holdings use SPDR GLD, the largest gold ETF, as a proxy for all gold ETFs. Central-bank purchases are those reported to the IMF; unreported buying estimated by the World Gold Council is not included.
Recalculated every 30 minutes from live dollar, gold and lira prices; bond yields update after the US close. The official signal (%1$s) changes only once a day; next evaluation %2$s.
